data.title: 3rd earnings upgrade in 2 decades: Jefferies lists stocks to play the trend
data.description:
Fiscal year 2026-27 (FY27) is trending differently, as India Inc. is set for its rare earnings upgrade. According to global investment bank Jefferies, MSCI India earnings estimates have historically been revised lower through the year, with downgrades in 18 of the past 20 completed fiscal years.
 
This time, Jefferies upgraded earnings per share (EPS) estimates by 1 per cent compared to the start of the fiscal year, making it only the third upgrade year in two decades, after FY12 (+1 per cent) and FY24 (+2 per cent). Economic growth has been revenue supportive, and we believe 4-year low margins could provide earnings support ahead.  
 
 
This, the brokerage said, is notable against an average c.10 per cent downgrade over FY07-26.  
 
"Revenue growth for Jefferies coverage ex-O&G/metals/financials accelerated for the fifth consecutive quarter to 21 per cent YoY in Sep’26, a 15-quarter high. This supported 19 per cent YoY earnings growth ex-O&G/metals despite EBITDA margins being near four-year lows. Going forward, while revenue growth may not accelerate further, we believe that margin improvements can provide support to earnings growth," Abhinav Sinha, along with other analysts, wrote in the Equity Strategy note shared on November 26.
 

Stocks to play upgrade cycle

Among sectors, the positive revisions within Jefferies coverage have been led by banks and non-banking finance companies (NBFCs), with 73 per cent and 71 per cent of stocks seeing FY27E EPS upgrades post Sep’26 results, while cyclical commodities (O&G, Metals) have also seen broad upgrades. 
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Sensex slumps 700 pts, Nifty below 25,700; Auto, IT down 1% each
 
Among stocks seeing consistent upgrades over the past two quarters, our preferred names include ICICI Bank, Kotak Bank, SBI, Bajaj Finance, Lodha, Lenskart, and Indian Hotels, said the investment bank. Reliance Industries and JSW Steel also stand out as preferred names where revision momentum has recently turned positive, it added.
 
On the flip side, Cement, Autos and IT saw higher downgrades post Sep’26 results. Among stocks with persistent downgrades over the past two quarters, where we have an Underperform rating, are LTM, Hyundai, Indus Towers, Tata Motors, TCS and Wipro, Jefferies noted.
 

Edge over EM peers

Jefferies also noted that India ranks first against its emerging market (EM) peers on earnings framework, as the potential slowdown in AI capex poses downside risks to Korea and Taiwan.
 
"While India’s EPS growth trails EM ex-AI majors (Samsung, SK hynix and TSMC) by 19ppt in CY26E/FY27E, it is expected to move to a 3ppt lead in CY27E/FY28E, pointing to an improving relative earnings outlook," it said.
 
Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: December income tax deadlines: TDS, advance tax, belated ITR and FAST-DS
data.description:
December has several important income tax deadlines, with taxpayers required to deposit tax deducted at source (TDS), pay the third instalment of advance tax and file belated income tax returns (ITRs) by the end of the month. Those with eligible foreign assets or income to disclose under the FAST-DS scheme also have a December 31 deadline.
 
Missing these dates could lead to interest, penalties or the loss of an opportunity to make a voluntary disclosure under a one-time scheme. Here are the deadlines taxpayers should keep track of.
 

December 7: Deposit TDS and TCS

Tax deducted or collected at source during November 2026 must be deposited with the Central Government by December 7.
 
 
Buyers covered under the applicable TCS provisions must also upload declarations received in Form 127 during November by this date. The form is relevant to specified transactions involving the collection of tax at source on goods.
 

December 15: Advance tax and TDS certificates

Two compliance requirements fall due on December 15.
 
Third advance tax instalment: Taxpayers whose estimated tax liability for Tax Year 2026–27, after adjusting TDS and TCS, is Rs 10,000 or more must pay advance tax in instalments. By December 15, at least 75 per cent of the estimated annual advance tax liability must have been paid cumulatively.
 
Form 132: Tax deductors must issue Form 132 for specified TDS deductions made during October 2026. These include transactions involving property purchases, rent, payments to contractors or professionals, and transfers of virtual digital assets (VDAs). The certificate helps recipients claim tax deducted while filing their returns.
 
Salaried taxpayers whose tax liability is fully covered by TDS generally do not need to pay advance tax separately.
 

December 30: Form 141 filing

Taxpayers responsible for specified TDS deductions made during November must furnish Form 141 by December 30.
 
The challan-cum-statement applies to specified transactions, including property purchases, rent, payments to contractors or professionals and transfers of virtual digital assets. It combines the reporting of deductions with the deposit of tax for covered transactions.
 

December 31: Belated ITR and FAST-DS

Belated ITR for AY 2026–27
 
Taxpayers who missed the original income tax return filing deadline for Assessment Year 2026–27 can file a belated return under Section 139(4) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, by December 31, 2026, or before the completion of assessment, whichever is earlier.
 
Filing late may attract a fee under Section 234F and interest under Section 234A, depending on the taxpayer's circumstances. Taxpayers should not wait until the last day to file, particularly if they need to correct information or reconcile tax credits.
 
FAST-DS declaration
 
The Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers – Disclosure Scheme (FAST-DS) is a one-time voluntary disclosure window for eligible taxpayers to declare specified foreign assets or income that was not disclosed earlier.
 
The Income Tax Department has set December 31, 2026, as the last date for filing Form 1 under the scheme. The scheme covers specified undisclosed foreign assets or income, as well as certain foreign assets acquired from explained sources but omitted from the relevant income tax return disclosures.
 
Eligible taxpayers should check the applicable category, declaration conditions and amount payable before filing. The scheme is not available in all cases, including certain assets or income linked to proceeds of crime or specified completed proceedings under the Black Money Act.
 
December's deadlines require taxpayers to track not just payments but also certificates and declarations. Filing or depositing tax on time can help avoid additional costs and ensure compliance with the applicable rules.

data.title: WBCHSE West Bengal HS Semester 3 Result 2027 to be out today on website
data.description:
West Bengal Council of Higher Secondary Education (WBCHSE) will declare the West Bengal HS Semester 3 Result 2027 today, November 27, 2026, online on the official result portal once the link is activated. 
 
As per the council's notification, the result will be released during a press conference at 2:30 PM at Vidyasagar Bhavan, Salt Lake, Kolkata. 
 
After that, students can view and download their provisional marksheets from 3:00 PM onwards. The WBCHSE HS Semester 3 Examination 2027 was held from September 21 to October 14, 2026. Most exams occurred in a single shift from 11:00 AM to 12:30 PM (1 hour 30 minutes). 
 

How to check the West Bengal HS 3rd Semester Result 2027?

Go to the official result website at result.wb.gov.in.
 
Search for the link for WB HS Semester 3 Result 2027 on the homepage.
 
Click on the result link.
 
Choose the Semester System option, if shown.
 
Fill in your examination roll number and registration number in the required fields.
 
Submit the login details.
 
Your West Bengal HS Semester 3 Result 2027 will be displayed on the screen. 
View your subject-wise marks and qualifying status.
 
Download the provisional marksheet and save it for later use.
 
Students are recommended to keep a printed copy of their online result until they obtain the original marksheet from their respective schools.

Details mentioned on WBCHSE HS Semester 3 Marksheet 2027

Student's Name
 
Examination Roll Number
 
Registration Number
 
Board Name
 
Examination Name
 
Subject-wise Marks
 
Qualifying Status. 

WB HS Semester 3 Result 2027: What happens after the result?

If students notice any errors in their personal information or exam scores, they must contact their individual schools or the relevant board officials to seek clarification. Those who successfully pass the examination can proceed with their studies in preparation for the next Semester IV exam. 
 
It is essential for students to stay updated on the council's notifications concerning the upcoming exam timetable and registration process. As per the council's annual working plan, online registration for the Semester IV and Semester III Supplementary Examination 2027 is set to occur from December 2 to 23, 2026.

data.title: SBI to increase lending under 'MSME Dream' to ₹50 crore by March 2027
data.description:
The State Bank of India (SBI) aims to increase lending under its 'MSME Dream' product, which gives small businesses collateral-free digital loans, to ₹50 crore by March 2027, a senior official said on Friday.

At present, the bank offers loans of up to ₹5 crore under the product launched in December 2023 and there has been some Closed User Group (CUG) selling of loans up to ₹10 crore at select branches, the official said.

"By November 30, we will increase the lending to ₹10 crore across all branches and will launch a pilot project to do loans of ₹50 crore each under the product on the same day," the official said.

 

The bank will increase the per loan borrowing under the product to ₹50 crore across all branches by March next year, the official said.

The country's largest lender has sanctioned ₹2.25 trillion under the 'Dream' product till now, the official said, stressing that the asset quality is also much better on such loans.

The gross Non-Performing Assets (NPA) ratio for loans under the product is under 0.50 per cent as against the level of over 1.50 per cent for the loans to the micro, small and medium enterprises, the official said.

A borrower fills in a set of details on a digital platform to check his or her credit worthiness, and a loan is sanctioned within 45 minutes by the engine, the official said.

Earlier, it used to take around a month to disburse a loan which has been now compressed to around a week using the digital inputs, he said.

data.title: Zaggle up 7% from day's low on inking deal with Yokohama, WSFX Global Pay
data.description:
Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services rebounded by 5.8 per cent from the day's low of ₹157.50 in Friday's intraday deals after the company announced signing a forex services agreement. The stock hit an intraday high of ₹168.18 on the NSE. At 1:45 PM, Zaggle pared gains and traded on a flat note at ₹162.67 on trades of around 40 lakh shares on the NSE. The stock hit a 52-week low at ₹146.65 on October 26, 2026, and a 52-week high of ₹397 was registered on November 28, 2025. Zaggle stock has witnessed a significant downturn since hitting a record high of ₹592 in September 2024. At current levels, the stock trades over 72 per cent lower compared to its peak, and down 53 per cent on a year-till-date basis. 

Zaggle inks 'Tripartite Agreement' with Yokohama and WSFX Global Pay

Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services in an exchange filing on Friday, said the company entered into a tripartite agreement with Yokohama Private Limited (Customer) and WSFX Global Pay Limited (WSFX). According to the terms of the agreement, Zaggle shall provide Expense Management System (EMS) to Yokohama, while WSFX shall act as the Authorised Dealer for forex services to Yokohama. Revenue from the agreement is variable in nature, and shall be in force for one year, unless terminated earlier. "The Quantum of fees is subjected to the number of international transactions made by the employees of the customer for the respective months on the Platform. "In such a case it would be difficult to ascertain the value/amount of the contract at this stage," Zaggle said in its release. Vijay Kedia bought stake in August Kedia Securities, owned by veteran investor Vijay Kishanlal Kedia, acquired 20 lakh shares, representing a 1.48 per cent stake in Zaggle in August. Kedia bought 20 lakh equity shares at ₹164.72 per share, for an aggregate consideration of approximately ₹32.94 crore. Equirus Securities has 'Long' rating on Zaggle Equirus Securities has a 'Long' rating on Zaggle with a price target of ₹275 per share by March 2028. The brokerage said, Zaggle's Q2FY27 revenue execeded its estimate by 2.8 per cent, while Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization (Ebitda) was in line. Zaggle's management expects EBITDA margins of 7-8 per cent and continue to prioritise cash conversion and disciplined capitalisation. "Around 65-70 per cent of DICE contracts have been novated, with the remaining transfers expected in 3QFY27. We see Zaggle well positioned to benefit from wider adoption of spend management solutions, while acquisitions strengthen client stickiness," said the brokerage. Even as Equirus maintained a 'Long' rating, the brokerage cut FY27/FY28 earnings estimates by 13.4 per cent/6.2 per cent citing moderate programme fee growth and the near-term profitability drag from DICE integration. "We expect technology expenses, DICE integration and Zagg.money losses to weigh on near-term margins and model a 7.8 per cent EBITDA margin for FY27E,", the brocaded added. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: India-US trade pact nears finish as pathway takes shape: Piyush Goyal
data.description:
The India-US trade deal is “close to culmination”, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Friday, indicating progress in negotiations days after Washington proposed a fresh tariff framework for Indian imports.
 
“The US trade deal is close to culmination. The process and pathway, which was always something which held back finalising the deal, is now taking some shape,” Goyal said while addressing the India Debt Capital Market Summit 2026 organised by TRUST Group.
 
His comments came after the US Trade Representative (USTR) proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods following a Section 301 investigation. Washington has indicated that the rate could be capped at 17 per cent if India and the US conclude a reciprocal trade agreement addressing the issues raised in the investigation.
 
 
India has disputed the US finding of structural excess capacity in its manufacturing industries and has said trade-related concerns should be addressed through bilateral trade negotiations.
 
Goyal also said the India-European Union free trade agreement was expected to be signed later this year and could come into effect by March or April 2027.
 
The minister said India's FTA coverage had expanded sharply over the past few years.
 
According to Goyal, before 2014, India's trade agreements covered economies with a combined gross domestic product (GDP) of about $10 trillion. Nine agreements finalised in the past four-and-a-half to five years, covering 38 developed countries, have added markets representing about $60 trillion of GDP.
 
Together, India's preferential market access now covers economies with around $70 trillion of GDP, he said.
 
Another eight or nine agreements under negotiation could add around $15 trillion, taking the total to about $85 trillion out of global GDP of $115-120 trillion, Goyal said.
 
“Almost every country in the world wants to do an FTA with India. We will add another $15 trillion. $85 trillion out of $115-120 trillion of global GDP will see India as a trusted partner; will see opportunities for India’s businesses to take forward,” he said.
 
On crude oil, Goyal said markets were sometimes too quick to re-rate or de-rate India based on relatively small movements in global prices.
 
While higher crude prices affected the economy, concerns that may have been significant in the 1990s or early 2000s needed to be viewed differently today given India's larger foreign exchange reserves, remittance flows, foreign direct investment and broader export base, he said.
 
“This could be an important matter of concern when we had much smaller foreign exchange reserves, much smaller remittances coming into the country, much less foreign direct investments coming into the country,” Goyal said.
 
A few dollars of movement in oil prices could not determine India's economic trajectory over the next two or three decades, he said, pointing to the country's expanding exports and economy.
 
The government said India had exported more than $700 billion annually and was targeting $1 trillion of goods and services exports in the current financial year.
 
Goyal also urged large companies, public sector undertakings and infrastructure developers to increasingly use the bond market as their first source of financing, including for long-duration capital expenditure.
 
He called for a broader investor base for long-term debt, asking insurers, pension and provident funds and mutual funds to increase participation in longer-duration instruments and look beyond only AAA-rated issuers.
 
The country's financing ecosystem would need to match the scale and duration of investments expected in areas such as semiconductor manufacturing, power grids, data centres and infrastructure over the coming decades, he said.
 
Goyal also urged exporters and their financiers to turn the market access created through FTAs into investment decisions by adding manufacturing capacity and preparing to serve newly opened markets.

data.title: Swiggy cuts 340 Instamart roles as quick-commerce unit restructures
data.description:
Swiggy's Instamart is cutting 340 jobs as it restructures for its next phase of growth, according to people familiar with the matter. 
 
Instamart is reshaping itself for its next phase of growth, factoring in Gen artificial intelligence (AI), new ways of working and how Instamart is organised, sources said. 
 
“This removes duplication, strengthens accountability and improves decision speed,” one of them added.
 
The cuts come during a period of growth at the unit, and they matter for investors because of that timing. In Q2 FY27, Instamart's gross order value (GOV) grew 16.7 per cent quarter-on-quarter (Q-o-Q) to ₹9,230 crore. Contribution margin improved 157 bps year-on-year (Y-o-Y) to -1.0 per cent of GOV over the same quarter, they said. “Profitability and growth remain at the centre of it,” one person said.
 
 
The reorganisation does not mean a pullback from operations, the people said. "Instamart will continue to invest in stores, supply chain and frontline teams," according to one of them.
 
The sources said there is a significant opportunity for Instamart to deepen its relationship with existing customers while continuing to expand reach. Instamart added a record 1.2 million monthly transacting users (MTUs) last quarter, they said. 
 
"There's considerable headroom in building a larger base of habitual customers, driving stronger retention and engagement, and increasing the frequency and value of transactions per customer, particularly across its key cities," one person said.
 
Instamart "is already seeing green shoots, driven in part by its Switch strategy," the people said. 
 
The Switch strategy is defined as Swiggy Instamart’s platform-wide differentiated assortment strategy designed around building avenues for customers to buy better as speed and price become table stakes in quick commerce.
 
For Swiggy, food is already profitable, the people said. Q2 saw the highest ever contribution margin, they said. In Q2 FY27 (the quarter ended September 30, 2026), Swiggy’s Food Delivery contribution margin improved to 7.7 per cent of GOV.
 
Toing, a standalone budget food delivery app launched by Swiggy, is bringing new customers into the category, according to the sources. Out-of-home consumption has also been profitable for seven consecutive quarters. Toing now operates in more than 50 cities, and two out of three new users on Toing were new to the food delivery category, the company said.
 
Swiggy remains well funded, according to the people. As of Q2, Swiggy has ₹13,500 crore in the bank, they said. 
 
Swiggy has put together a comprehensive assistance package for transitioning employees, the sources said. It includes severance support in addition to statutory payouts. Employee stock option plan ( ESOP) vesting has been accelerated through the last working day, according to the people.
 
Health insurance and wellness subscription have been extended until May 2027, the sources said. Relocation support is available for eligible employees.  Outplacement support includes 3 months of premium access to career and networking tools, they said.
 
In October, Swiggy reported a 15.6 per cent Y-o-Y decline in its net loss to ₹922 crore for the September quarter, from ₹1,092 crore a year earlier.
 
The company had posted a loss of ₹791 crore in the previous quarter.
 
Revenue from operations rose 36 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹7,571 crore in the second quarter of 2026-27, compared with ₹5,561 crore a year earlier. Revenue stood at ₹6,812 crore in the previous quarter.
 
Swiggy's total expenses rose nearly 30 per cent year on year to ₹8,703 crore in the quarter ended September, from ₹6,711 crore a year earlier. Expenses stood at ₹7,813 crore in the preceding quarter.
 
"Our Food delivery business delivered its highest ever profits and margins while we continue to unlock new
 
category growth through Toing, our standalone oﬀering for aﬀordable meals,” Sriharsha Majety, managing director (MD) and Group chief executive officer (CEO), Swiggy, had said.
 
GOV of the food delivery business grew 17.7 per cent Y-o-Y and 5.9 per cent Q-o-Q to ₹10,054 crore, the company said in a press release. 
 
The company added 69 dark stores during the quarter, taking the total to 1,240 stores covering 5.2 million sq ft, up 13.3 per cent year on year. Contribution stood at -1.0 per cent of GOV, up 157 basis points year on year and down 82 basis points Q-o-Q. 
The quick-commerce business's adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) margin improved to -9.7 per cent from -9.8 per cent in the previous quarter, with an overall loss of ₹895 crore for the quarter.
 
“We believe that diﬀerentiation will decide winners with speed and selection becoming table stakes.We see assortment as a curation game rather than a volume game, and our aim is to enable consumers to buy better, not just oﬀer more,” Majety had said.

data.title: Jefferies sees telecom tariff hike in April next year; Airtel top pick
data.description:
Brokerage Jefferies expects telecom operators to undertake the next round of tariff hikes in April 2027, and sees the sector revenue growing at a CAGR of 13 per cent over FY27-FY29 to $44 billion.
 
The brokerage said that Bharti Airtel and Bharti Hexacom are its preferred picks in the sector, and assigned targets of ₹2,380 and ₹2,080, respectively.
 
Jefferies, in its note, said that the sector's annualised revenues reached a new high of $35 billion in Q2FY27, up 8.5 per cent Y-o-Y, even in the absence of tariff hikes. The growth was supported almost equally by subscriber growth (+4.1 per cent Y-o-Y) and ARPU expansion (+4.3 per cent Y-o-Y).
 
 
All market categories contributed incremental revenues Y-o-Y, Jefferies said, adding that Bharti Airtel continued to outperform, accounting for around 50 per cent of incremental revenues and delivered double-digit revenue growth in 9 of 22 circles. It gained 70 bps market share, while Vodafone Idea lost market share by 55 bps.
 
"Sustained high-single-digit growth in the absence of tariff hikes provides comfort on the sector's underlying growth trajectory, supported by continued premiumisation and subscriber additions," the brokerage said.
 
Jefferies said Airtel reported a 10 per cent Y-o-Y increase in its revenue in Q2, ahead of the sector, driven by 7 per cent ARPU growth and 3 per cent subscriber growth. The ARPU growth remained ahead of peers, reflecting its continued focus on premiumisation and quality subscriber additions.
 
"Its ability to consistently grow ahead of the industry reinforces its strong positioning across both urban and rural markets," the brokerage said.
 
For Bharti Airtel, key downside risks include the absence of tariff hikes, higher-than-expected capital expenditure, lower-than-expected 5G monetisation and market-share gains.
 
For Bharti Hexacom, Jefferies said that risks include delays in tariff increases, a lower quantum of hikes, intensifying competition, and the impact of related-party transactions on future margins.
 
Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: Samay Raina makes YouTube history with 1 million paid channel members
data.description:
Indian comedian Samay Raina has become the first YouTube creator globally to cross one million channel members, setting a new record on the platform. YouTube confirmed the feat and shared it in a post on the Google India blog. 
 
The achievement comes as Raina rebuilds his career following the controversy surrounding India's Got Latent in February 2025.
 
Raina currently has more than 12.4 million subscribers on YouTube. However, the one-million milestone refers to paid channel memberships, through which viewers financially support creators in exchange for exclusive content and other benefits.

Youtube on Samay Raina’s one million milestone

Praising Samay's journey, the YouTube team mentioned, “From host-level banter with Grandmasters to creating the phenomenon that is India's Got Latent, Samay turned his YouTube channel into the ultimate virtual hangout for millions.”
 
 
It added, “Samay's 1-million-channel-member landmark captures a much bigger cultural moment happening across India right now. Audiences aren't just watching from the sidelines anymore; they're choosing to show up for their favourite creators in deeply personal, meaningful ways. In June 2026 alone, more than 1.2 million fans in India bought at least one channel membership on YouTube, driving a 25%+ year-over-year jump in membership revenue for Indian creators.”
 
The platform also emphasised the increasing trend of paid channel memberships among creators in India. “It's an extraordinary moment for Samay and a proud moment for India's entire creator ecosystem. Congratulations, Samay! We can't wait to see what hilarious, high-energy concept you bring to life next,” the post added.

Samay Raina’s comeback

Raina's latest achievement follows a turbulent phase in his career after India's Got Latent became embroiled in controversy in February 2025. This situation resulted in multiple police filings and FIRs against various individuals connected to the specific episode. 
 
In response, Samay Raina issued an apology and deleted all episodes from the initial season on his YouTube channel. He made a comeback in 2026 with his stand-up special Still Alive, where he spoke about the “difficult period”. Eventually, he reintroduced India's Got Latent with a season 2, which debuted on both YouTube and Netflix.
 
Samay said, "I was depressed when we were in Canada. I used to ask ChatGPT, ‘When do you think Samay Raina will ever be able to bring his show back?’ ChatGPT would reply, ‘It's unclear right now’. Then I used to write, ‘Please say yes.’ I had no idea that the show would come back in this manner." 
ALSO READ: Hanuman Ansh OTT release: When and where to watch spiritual biopic online?

Who is Samay Raina?

Samay Raina is an Indian stand-up comedian, YouTuber and chess enthusiast. He rose to prominence after winning the second season of the comedy reality show Comicstaan, alongside Aakash Gupta.
 
He later gained widespread popularity through his YouTube content, chess streams and comedy talent show India's Got Latent, which became one of the most talked-about digital shows in India. 
ALSO READ: 27-year-old Jennifer Barreto from Puerto Rico crowned Miss Universe 2026

data.title: X rolls out parental controls for teens, but parents face a limitation
data.description:
Social media platform X has introduced parental controls for teenage accounts, allowing parents and guardians to monitor screen time, approve new followers and restrict content recommendations. However, the new features come with a limitation that teenagers must agree to link their accounts with those of their parents before supervision can begin.
 
The announcement, made by X's official Safety account, marks the platform's introduction of dedicated parental supervision tools. The features are designed for users aged 13 to 17 and give parents some control over their children's activity without granting them access to private conversations or browsing histories.

How will X's parental controls work?

Parents and guardians can link their accounts with those of their teenagers through an invitation. The teenager must accept the request before the parental controls can be activated. The invitation remains valid for 72 hours.
 
 
Once the accounts are linked, parents can view how much time their teenager has spent on X over the previous seven days and set daily screen-time limits. They can also restrict access to certain features and manage aspects of their children's interactions on the platform.
 
X allows parents to require approval before new accounts can follow their teenagers. Enabling this option also makes the teenager's account private.
 
Parents can additionally restrict recommendations and videos in the For You feed to accounts their teenagers already follow. They can filter content by blocking specific words and switch off the display of sensitive media. ALSO READ: WhatsApp partners with Jio, Verizon, more to bring travel eSIM data plans

Parents can restrict DMs, but cannot read private messages

The new controls allow parents to decide who can send direct messages to their teenagers. They can also see which accounts their children have exchanged one-to-one messages with.
 
However, parents will not be able to read the actual conversations. They will also not have access to their teenagers' search or viewing histories, or be able to post on their behalf or take control of their accounts. 
ALSO READ: Apple removes Chinese AI chatbot from App Store over child safety concerns

Teenagers can refuse parental supervision

One of the key limitations of the new feature is that parents cannot activate supervision without their teenagers' consent.
 
The teenager must accept the invitation sent by the parent before the accounts can be linked. This gives teenagers the option to decline parental supervision, even if their parents want to enable the controls.
 
A parent can supervise up to five teenage accounts, while each teenager can be linked to only one parent or guardian.

What happens when teenagers turn 18?

The parental supervision arrangement is intended for users aged 13 to 17. The supervision link automatically ends when the teenager turns 18.
